text:
alex: Heads up — several CI deploy jobs started failing with 403 partway through. Appears ephemeral SA tokens expired earlier than the runner expected. Example job id: gitlab-runner/12345. Anyone seen this behavior?

priya: Can you paste the runner logs and any token exp claim you can grab?

alex: Log snippet below (redacted):
```
2026-03-17T08:50:12Z runner-proxy: request id=req-9a1b2c token=impersonation ci-runner-sa@project -> 403 Unauthorized (impersonation window expired)
2026-03-17T08:50:12Z job: build-12345 failed after 312s
```
Token payload we pulled from the proxy (exp in unix): `exp: 4281099940` but runner tried to use it at `4281100000` and got rejected.

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) TTL "envelope" drift — the proxy issues tokens with slightly shorter expiry than requested under heavy load, 2) clock skew / tight refresh loop causing overlapping refreshes and a stale token cache. We had a kube node pool rolling restart ~2h ago which might explain some clock drift.

alex: This popped up across eu-west1 and us-central though, so not just one node.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-123 triggered — high-severity: CI deploys failing with 403 impersonation errors. PagerDuty notified.

priya: Can you grab the audit log trace for one of the failed impersonations and paste the trace id? Also, if you can reproduce, try adding a local clock check: `date -u +%s` on runner and proxy.

alex: Audit snippet (redacted):
```
protoPayload.methodName: "google.iam.credentials.v1.IAMCredentials.GenerateAccessToken"
resourceName: "projects/-/serviceAccounts/ci-runner-sa@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
requestMetadata.callerIp: "35.XXX.YYY.ZZZ"
response.status.code: 7
trace: "trace-pkt-9a1b2c"
```
Runner node clock: `4281100005`, proxy server: `4281099974`. ~31s skew.

sam: That skew + tight refresh explains it — if the proxy issues token with requested TTL then the proxy's clock lags, the token's `exp` ends up earlier relative to runner clock. Also seen singleflight/race where multiple refreshes create short-lived tokens in the cache. Quick repro I ran locally:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..5}; do
  tok=$(gcloud auth print-identity-token --audiences=iam --format=json)
  exp=$(echo $tok | jq -r '.exp')
  echo "issued exp=$exp now=$(date +%s)"
  sleep 1
done
```
Run in tight loop and you can see small negative margins when server clock is behind.

michael: Long-term fix: make token issuance singleflight (no duplicate concurrent issuance), add a min-remaining-time guard on the runner client (e.g., require >=180s left before using token), and add a small issuance buffer on the proxy (subtract 30s from requested TTL when server clock might be behind).

alex: For now, what's the safest immediate workaround? Increase token lifetime?

priya: Don't increase lifetime as a first resort — that expands blast radius. Temporary mitigation rolled out: patched runners to refuse tokens with <120s remaining and bumped proxy cache TTL floor to 600s to avoid constant reissue. Also pushed a small clock-sync check alert to node provisioning. That reduced failures in the last 10m.

ci-deployer-bot: Rollback of deployer service to v2.14.3 completed at 2026-03-17T09:12:00 (automated rollback due to pipeline failures).

alex: Thanks — I'll open a support ticket to notify customers impacted and collate which jobs failed. Also tagging SRE for a postmortem on why the node pool clocks diverged.

sam: I'll open a MR with singleflight + min-expiry check for the proxy and runner: gl/ci-runner#4578. Will also add e2e that simulates clock skew.

priya: FYI: we'll add a monitoring rule for token margin <60s across proxies and runners.

alex: Good plan. Will follow up with incident notes once SRE posts the postmortem. Thanks all.
